title: Inner preparation run
statement: Let $C,e,n$ be natural numbers, let the mode be Boolean, let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words, let $h$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $v$ assign natural numbers to fourteen registers. Suppose every register value is at most $8(2C+3)(|h|+1)^{e+1}$, register $4$ equals $4n+4$, registers $6,7,10,11$ are zero, and $n\le |h|$. Starting in the inner-preparation state with no result, the computation reaches the length-bound state with registers $8$ and $7$ equal to $n+1$ and $C(n+1)^e$, respectively, and every other register unchanged. Every configuration before the final one satisfies the prescribed invariant: the instruction is admissible at that configuration and all register values are at most $8(2C+3)(|h|+1)^{e+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a function from finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words
$v$ assigns natural numbers to fourteen registers, each at most $8(2C+3)(|h|+1)^{e+1}$
replaced:
Let $C,e,h,n$ be natural numbers or bit strings as appropriate, let the mode be Boolean,
let $f$ be a function on bit strings, and let $v$ assign natural numbers to fourteen
registers. Suppose every register value is at most $8(2C+3)(|h|+1)^{e+1}$; register $4$
equals $4n+4$; registers $6,7,10,11$ are zero; and $n\le |h|$. Then the machine reaches
the length-bound state from the inner-preparation state, with registers $8$ and $7$
updated to $n+1$ and $C(n+1)^e$, respectively, and all other registers unchanged; the
prescribed configuration invariant holds throughout the run.
